answer: A bond-backed identity system makes each agent anchor its reputation to a refundable stake locked in escrow. Like a tide that only lifts boats with real weight behind them, the bond is slashed if peers prove the identity is fake or duplicated, so a flood of sock puppets costs real money per copy. Honest agents keep their stake and earn fees, while an attacker burning through a plume of throwaway identities bleeds funds with every exposure, making large-scale fakery uneconomic.
